candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care, Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement), printed p.22 / PDF p.25: define performance improvement/quality assurance activities; participate in performance improvement projects and quality improvement processes; utilize research and other references for performance improvement actions
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement) / root-cause analysis tool selection
candidate.educational_objective: Differentiate the 5 Whys root-cause technique from other quality-improvement methods by recognizing its repeated causal questioning from an observed problem toward underlying causes.

options.A: Ask why repeatedly, using each answer to probe the next causal layer until the team reaches the underlying cause or causes
options.B: Map the process and identify possible failure modes before another adverse event occurs
options.C: Plot error rates over time to distinguish common-cause from special-cause variation
options.D: Test a small workflow change, study the results, and adapt the next test based on what is learned

candidate.rationale: IHI describes the 5 Whys as repeatedly asking why an event occurred and continuing to ask why based on successive answers until the underlying root cause is reached; IHI also notes that a problem may have more than one root cause. Therefore A is the best answer. B describes the proactive logic of Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA), C describes use of a control chart to examine process variation over time, and D describes a Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) cycle for testing change. Each distractor is a legitimate quality-improvement method, but none is the 5 Whys technique.
candidate.source_claim_supported: The 5 Whys technique identifies underlying root causes by repeatedly asking why successive causal explanations occurred; multiple root causes may exist.
candidate.source_locator: Main page text and section 'Ask Why? Five Times': ask 'Why did this happen?' and continue asking 'Why?' again and again until reaching the root cause; page also notes that a problem may have multiple root causes
candidate.source_version_date: Current undated IHI web tool page; accessed 2026-08-17
